public_rationale: For July–September 2024, Microsoft reported $20 billion in capital expenditure including finance leases and $14.9 billion in cash purchases of property and equipment [e1]. Its discussion combines cloud and AI spending without allocating expenditure specifically to generative AI and associated infrastructure [e1]. These quarterly figures neither establish spending above $200 billion nor provide a comprehensive total at or below that threshold for December 3, 2023–December 2, 2024 [e1].
limitations: The disclosure covers one company and one quarter, not the industry over the contracted twelve-month period [e1].
The figures do not isolate spending on generative AI and its associated infrastructure [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Capital expenditures on generative AI and infrastructure exceeded $200 billion in the last year.

statement.excerpt: Remember, the capital expenditures on generative AI and the associated infrastructure have gone over $200 billion in the last year.

from_speaker: capital expenditures on generative AI and the associated infrastructure
our_interpretation: Read 'the last year' as the twelve months immediately preceding publication, December 3, 2023 through December 2, 2024.
The ordinary reading concerns spending already incurred, not announced budgets or future commitments.
Associated infrastructure includes infrastructure supporting generative AI. Counting all corporate capital expenditure requires evidence that it serves this purpose.
The statement identifies neither an accounting basis nor a defined group of companies.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable expenditure records establish more than USD 200 billion of realized generative-AI and associated infrastructure capital expenditure during the target period, without double counting.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive, comparable accounting establishes a total no greater than USD 200 billion during that period.
